summary: The version-number rule in looksLikeAtFilename accepts any letters as the final label, so real addresses whose domain is two or more all-number labels plus a real domain ending (bob@1.2.com, jane@163.126.net) are no longer flagged by pii.email. The file-extension rule already covers names like terminal-bench@2.0.json, so the version rule only needs to cover extensions that are also domain endings.
evidence: return NON_TLD_EXTENSION.test(domain) || /^\d+(?:\.\d+)+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/.test(domain); a scratch script calling scan(s,{repoVisibility:'private'}) printed [] (no findings) for both "mail bob@1.2.com" and "mail jane@163.126.net".

summary: The version-style branch of looksLikeAtFilename treats any domain made of two or more number-only parts plus one ending as a filename, so real-looking addresses at number-only subdomains no longer report pii.email.
evidence: return NON_TLD_EXTENSION.test(domain) || /^\d+(?:\.\d+)+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/.test(domain); scratch probe: scan('mail sales@24.7.media') => [], scan('ops@10.0.co') => []

summary: isNumericConstant exempts the exact digits regardless of the surrounding words, so a bare number that is also a valid-looking US phone number (2147483647, 2147483648, 8589934592, 2166136261) is not flagged even after 'phone:' or 'call me at'.
evidence: validate: ... !isNumericConstant(span) ...; scratch probe: scan('call me at 2147483647') => [], scan('phone: 2147483648') => []
